existing_eitza_edge.proof: הַנּוֹתֵן צְדָקָה נִצּוֹל מֵעֲבֵרוֹת. כִּי 'כָּל הַמְרַחֵם עַל הַבְּרִיּוֹת מְרַחֲמִין עָלָיו מִן הַשָּׁמַיִם', 'וְכָל מִי שֶׁאֵין בּוֹ דֵּעָה אָסוּר לְרַחֵם עָלָיו', וְכֵיוָן שֶׁמְּרַחֲמִין עָלָיו בְּהֶכְרֵחַ נוֹתְנִין לוֹ דַּעַת. וַאֲזַי נִצּוֹל מִלָּבוֹא לִידֵי עֲבֵרָה, כִּי 'אֵין אָדָם עוֹבֵר עֲבֵרָה אֶלָּא אִם כֵּן נִכְנַס בּוֹ רוּחַ שְׁטוּת', אֲבָל כְּשֶׁיֵּשׁ לוֹ דֵּעָה נִצּוֹל מֵעֲבֵרוֹת.

bechina_language_scan.notes: None of these markers appear anywhere in the 3-line source text. The Torah is a compact syllogism using 'כִּי' (because/for), 'וְכֵיוָן שֶׁ' (and since/therefore), 'אֶלָּא אִם כֵּן' (unless), and 'אֲבָל' (but) — all of which are logical connectives indicating causality and conditionality, not parallel-nature identity.

concepts_examined_and_excluded.reason: Giving charity is the ACT that generates compassion from heaven. The relationship is directional — צדקה (charity/justice) produces or demonstrates רחמים (compassion) but the two are not identified as sharing the same essential nature in this Torah. The Torah does not say 'charity IS compassion' or 'charity is an aspect of compassion' — it says 'one who shows compassion [through charity] receives compassion [from heaven]'. This is reciprocal causality, not bechina.

Daat (knowledge/awareness) and ruach shtut (spirit of foolishness) are opposites — their relationship is one of mutual exclusion, not bechina identity. The Torah states that sin only enters when ruach shtut is present AND that daat prevents this. This is a logical contrapositive structure (if no daat → ruach shtut can enter; if daat is present → ruach shtut cannot enter), not a shared-nature identification. One could argue they are 'mirror concepts' but neither the text nor standard bechina convention treats logical opposites-as-mirrors as bechina edges — they would require explicit equating language.

In the absence of explicit bechina language, this should be classified as contextual elaboration rather than a formal bechina edge.

eitza_chain_structure.description: The full eitza (causal) chain of Torah #116, which accounts for all the conceptual content of this Torah:

chain.mechanism: Talmudic principle: Shabbat 151b — measure for measure, one who shows compassion receives compassion
Talmudic principle: Berakhot 33 — one who lacks daat it is forbidden to have compassion on him; therefore heavenly compassion necessarily brings the gift of daat
Talmudic principle: Sotah 3a — a person only sins if a spirit of foolishness (ruach shtut) enters him; one who has daat is protected from the spirit of foolishness and therefore from sin

eitza_chain_structure.note: All three steps are eitza relationships. The dataset correctly captures only one edge (the summary eitza: הנותן צדקה → נצול מעברות). The intermediate steps (steps 1 and 2) could be added as additional eitza edges but are not needed for bechina/package analysis.
